messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

The inbox is getting busy. Let staff mark tickets `normal` or `high` priority; default to normal.
Add priority to the existing ticket responses and updates, and let staff combine filters:

```http
GET /api/v1/tickets?status=open&assignee_id=unassigned&priority=high&q=receipt
```

Support status, assignee, requester, and priority filters, plus `q` for a case-insensitive search
through subjects and public comments. Use `assignee_id` and `requester_id` for people; `unassigned`
means nobody is assigned. Search should treat what the user types as literal text.
Customers can filter their own requests by status. Priority is internal.

# frozen_string_literal: true

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets

  has_many :comments, class_name: "TicketComment", dependent: :delete_all, inverse_of: :ticket

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_is_active_staff_in_account, if: -> { assignee_id.present? && (new_record? || will_save_change_to_assignee_id?) }

  before_create :initialize_public_updated_at
  before_update :sync_public_updated_at

  scope :recently_active_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :recently_publicly_active_first, -> { order(public_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  def open?
    status == "open"
  end

  def pending?
    status == "pending"
  end

  def solved?
    status == "solved"
  end

  private

  def initialize_public_updated_at
    now = Time.current
    self.created_at ||= now
    self.updated_at ||= now
    self.public_updated_at ||= updated_at
  end

  def sync_public_updated_at
    return unless will_save_change_to_status? || will_save_change_to_subject?

    now = Time.current
    self.updated_at = now
    self.public_updated_at = now
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return unless requester && account_id

    if requester.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same account")
    end
  end

  def assignee_is_active_staff_in_account
    return if assignee_id.nil?

    if assignee.nil? || assignee.account_id != account_id || !assignee.staff? || assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member in this account")
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

class TicketComment < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :ticket, inverse_of: :comments
  belongs_to :author, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :ticket_comments

  attr_accessor :skip_ticket_touch

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :public, inclusion: { in: [ true, false ] }
  validate :associations_belong_to_account

  after_create :touch_ticket, unless: :skip_ticket_touch

  scope :public_only, -> { where(public: true) }
  scope :oldest_first, -> { order(created_at: :asc, id: :asc) }

  private

  def touch_ticket
    return unless ticket&.persisted?

    now = Time.current
    if public?
      ticket.update_columns(updated_at: now, public_updated_at: now)
    else
      ticket.update_columns(updated_at: now)
    end
  end

  def associations_belong_to_account
    return unless account_id

    if ticket && ticket.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:ticket, "must belong to the same account")
    end

    if author && author.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:author, "must belong to the same account")
    end
  end
end

            status: "open"

          ticket: ticket,
          author: current_user,
          body: comment_params&.permit(:body)&.[](:body),
          public: true,
          skip_ticket_touch: true
        )

        ticket_valid = ticket.valid?
        comment_valid = comment.valid?

          render_validation_errors(errors)

        comment_params = optional_hash_param(request_params, :comment)

module Api
  module V1
    class RequestsController < BaseController
      before_action :require_account!
      before_action :authenticate_user!
      before_action :require_active_account!
      before_action :set_request, only: %i[show update comments]

      def index
        result = paginate(own_tickets.recently_publicly_active_first)
        render json: {
          requests: result[:records].map { |ticket| serialize_request(ticket) }
        }.merge(result[:meta]), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        render json: { request: serialize_request(@ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      def create
        request_params = require_hash_param(params, :request)
        comment_params = optional_hash_param(request_params, :comment)

        ticket = current_account.tickets.build(
          request_params.permit(:subject).merge(
            requester: current_user,
            status: "open"
          )
        )

        comment = TicketComment.new(
          account: current_account,
          ticket: ticket,
          author: current_user,
          body: comment_params&.permit(:body)&.[](:body),
          public: true,
          skip_ticket_touch: true
        )

        ticket_valid = ticket.valid?
        comment_valid = comment.valid?

        unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
          errors = ticket.errors.to_hash
          errors[:comment] = comment.errors.to_hash if comment.errors.any?
          render_validation_errors(errors)
          return
        end

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          ticket.save!
          comment.save!
        end

        render json: { request: serialize_request(ticket) }, status: :created
      end

      def update
        request_params = require_hash_param(params, :request)
        comment_params = optional_hash_param(request_params, :comment)

        errors = {}

        status_provided = request_params.key?(:status)
        requested_status = request_params[:status]
        if status_provided && requested_status != "solved"
          errors[:status] = [ "can only be set to solved" ]
        end

        comment = nil
        if comment_params
          comment = TicketComment.new(
            account: current_account,
            ticket: @ticket,
            author: current_user,
            body: comment_params.permit(:body)[:body],
            public: true
          )
          unless comment.valid?
            errors[:comment] = comment.errors.to_hash
          end
        end

        if errors.any?
          render_validation_errors(errors)
          return
        end

        if status_provided && requested_status == "solved"
          @ticket.status = "solved"
        elsif comment && (@ticket.pending? || @ticket.solved?)
          @ticket.status = "open"
        end

        unless @ticket.valid?
          render_validation_errors(@ticket.errors.to_hash)
          return
        end

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          @ticket.save! if @ticket.changed?
          comment&.save!
        end

        render json: { request: serialize_request(@ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      def comments
        result = paginate(@ticket.comments.public_only.includes(:author).oldest_first)
        render json: {
          comments: result[:records].map { |comment| serialize_comment(comment) }
        }.merge(result[:meta]), status: :ok
      end

      private

      def own_tickets
        current_account.tickets.where(requester: current_user)
      end

      def set_request
        @ticket = find_scoped_record(own_tickets, params[:id])
        return if @ticket

        render_error("Request not found", code: "not_found", status: :not_found)
      end
    end
  end

          tickets: result[:records].map { |ticket| serialize_ticket(ticket) }
        }.merge(result[:meta]), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        render json: { ticket: serialize_ticket(@ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      def update
        ticket_params = require_hash_param(params, :ticket)
        comment_params = optional_hash_param(ticket_params, :comment)

        errors = {}

        status_provided = ticket_params.key?(:status)
        requested_status = ticket_params[:status]
        if status_provided
          if requested_status.is_a?(String) && Ticket::STATUSES.include?(requested_status)
            @ticket.status = requested_status
          else
            errors[:status] = [ "is not included in the list" ]
          end
        end

        if ticket_params.key?(:assignee_id)
          raw_assignee_id = ticket_params[:assignee_id]
          if raw_assignee_id.nil?
            @ticket.assignee = nil
          else
            parsed_id = parse_assignee_id(raw_assignee_id)
            assignee = parsed_id ? current_account.users.staff.active.find_by(id: parsed_id) : nil
            if assignee
              @ticket.assignee = assignee
            else
              errors[:assignee_id] = [ "must be an active staff member in this account" ]
            end
          end
        end

        comment = nil
        if comment_params
          comment_errors = {}

          raw_body = comment_params[:body]
          body_value = raw_body.is_a?(String) ? raw_body : nil
          if !raw_body.nil? && !raw_body.is_a?(String)
            comment_errors[:body] = [ "must be a string" ]
          end

          if comment_params.key?(:public)
            raw_public = comment_params[:public]
            if raw_public == true || raw_public == false
              is_public = raw_public
            else
              comment_errors[:public] = [ "must be a boolean" ]
              is_public = true
            end
          else
            is_public = true
          end

          comment = TicketComment.new(
            account: current_account,
            ticket: @ticket,
            author: current_user,
            body: body_value,
            public: is_public
          )

          unless comment.valid?
            comment.errors.to_hash.each do |key, messages|
              comment_errors[key] ||= messages
            end
          end

          errors[:comment] = comment_errors if comment_errors.any?
        end

        if errors.any?
          render_validation_errors(errors)
          return
        end

        unless @ticket.valid?
          render_validation_errors(@ticket.errors.to_hash)
          return
        end

        ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
          @ticket.save! if @ticket.changed?
          comment&.save!
        end

        render json: { ticket: serialize_ticket(@ticket) }, status: :ok
      end

      def comments
        result = paginate(@ticket.comments.includes(:author).oldest_first)
        render json: {
          comments: result[:records].map { |comment| serialize_comment(comment) }
        }.merge(result[:meta]), status: :ok
      end

      private

      def parse_assignee_id(raw)
        if raw.is_a?(Integer)
          return (raw > 0 && raw <= MAX_BIGINT) ? raw : nil
        end

        if raw.is_a?(String)
          str = raw.strip
          return nil unless str.match?(/\A[1-9][0-9]*\z/)

          value = str.to_i
          return (value > 0 && value <= MAX_BIGINT) ? value : nil
        end

        nil
      end

      def set_ticket
        @ticket = find_scoped_record(current_account.tickets.includes(:requester, :assignee), params[:id])
        return if @ticket

        render_error("Ticket not found", code: "not_found", status: :not_found)
      end
    end
  end

ENV["RAILS_ENV"] ||= "test"
require_relative "../config/environment"
require "rails/test_help"

require "uri"

module ActiveSupport
  class TestCase
    setup do
      ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    end

    def with_env(overrides)
      originals = {}
      overrides.each do |key, value|
        key_s = key.to_s
        originals[key_s] = ENV.key?(key_s) ? ENV[key_s] : :__unset__
        if value.nil?
          ENV.delete(key_s)
        else
          ENV[key_s] = value
        end
      end
      yield
    ensure
      originals.each do |key_s, original|
        if original == :__unset__
          ENV.delete(key_s)
        else
          ENV[key_s] = original
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

module ApiTestHelper
  def json_body
    JSON.parse(response.body)
  end

  def account_headers(subdomain, token: nil, extra: {})
    headers = {
      "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain,
      "Accept" => "application/json"
    }
    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token
    headers.merge(extra)
  end

  def extract_link_from_mail(mail, path:)
    body = mail.body.decoded
    match = body.match(%r{https?://[^\s]+#{Regexp.escape(path)}\?[^\s]+})
    assert_not_nil match, "Expected link containing #{path} in mail body:\n#{body}"
    match[0]
  end

  def extract_query_params(url)
    uri = URI.parse(url)
    URI.decode_www_form(uri.query.to_s).to_h
  end

  def create_account_via_api(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    post "/api/v1/account/create",
      params: {
        account: {
          name: name,
          subdomain: subdomain,
          admin: {
            name: admin_name,
            email: email,
            password: password
          }
        }
      },
      as: :json
  end

  def register_customer_via_api(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password")
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
      params: {
        user: {
          name: name,
          email: email,
          password: password
        }
      },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain),
      as: :json
  end

  def verify_last_email!(subdomain:)
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_not_nil mail, "Expected a verification email to have been sent"
    link = extract_link_from_mail(mail, path: "/verify-email")
    params = extract_query_params(link)
    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
      params: { email_verification: { token: params["token"] } },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain),
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    params["token"]
  end

  def sign_in_via_api(subdomain:, email:, password:)
    post "/api/v1/sessions",
      params: { session: { email: email, password: password } },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain),
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    json_body.dig("session", "token")
  end

  def invite_staff_via_api(subdomain: "acme", token:, email:, role: "agent")
    post "/api/v1/invitations",
      params: { invitation: { email: email, role: role } },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain, token: token),
      as: :json
  end

  def extract_last_invitation_token
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_not_nil mail, "Expected an invitation email to have been sent"
    link = extract_link_from_mail(mail, path: "/accept-invitation")
    extract_query_params(link)["token"]
  end

  def accept_invitation_via_api(subdomain: "acme", token:, name:, password:)
    post "/api/v1/invitation_acceptances",
      params: {
        invitation_acceptance: {
          token: token,
          name: name,
          password: password
        }
      },
      headers: account_headers(subdomain),
      as: :json

module ActiveSupport
  class TestCase
    setup do

    def with_env(overrides)
      originals = {}
      overrides.each do |key, value|
        key_s = key.to_s
        originals[key_s] = ENV.key?(key_s) ? ENV[key_s] : :__unset__
        if value.nil?
          ENV.delete(key_s)
        else
          ENV[key_s] = value
        end
      end
      yield
    ensure

        if original == :__unset__
          ENV.delete(key_s)
        else
          ENV[key_s] = original
        end
      end
    end
  end

module ApiTestHelper
  def json_body
    JSON.parse(response.body)
  end

  def account_headers(subdomain, token: nil, extra: {})
    headers = {
      "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain,
      "Accept" => "application/json"
    }
    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token
    headers.merge(extra)
  end

    body = mail.body.decoded
    match = body.match(%r{https?://[^\s]+#{Regexp.escape(path)}\?[^\s]+})

  end

  def extract_query_params(url)

Alright, let's break this down systematically. I see a consistent pattern in how parameters are handled across the codebase, particularly concerning data validation for attributes like `priority` and `status` in the `TicketsController`. Errors are returned with a 422 Unprocessable Content status, which is the correct response for invalid input, and the process consistently rolls back changes to the ticket - crucial for maintaining data integrity.

I also see that omitting a parameter preserves the existing value, which is important. Combining filters like `status`, `assignee_id`, and `priority` seems straightforward within the `PATCH`/`PUT /api/v1/tickets/:id` requests.

The distinction between customer and staff endpoints is crystal clear. Customer requests (`GET /api/v1/requests`, `POST /api/v1/requests`, `PATCH /api/v1/requests/:id`) are designed to ignore internal attributes, a security measure, which is the correct approach to prevent information leakage. Internal attributes such as `priority` can't be set or filtered by customers (they are effectively ignored), and only the staff has control over this attribute. This is clearly by design.

**Diving Deeper into Filtering**

Now, filtering on `GET /api/v1/requests`. It appears that customers are limited to filtering by `status` only, and the handling of invalid values for this filter is rigorous, mirroring the pattern observed in other controllers. Importantly, other parameters are completely ignored, and this is exactly what's required by the customer use case. This is a very clean approach and maintains a simple API surface. This means that passing an invalid status or an attribute that should not be visible or filterable to customers leads to the correct result - a 422 error.

**Staff Filtering & Search - The Key**

Now, the staff `GET /api/v1/tickets`. This is where it gets interesting, as staff should be able to filter by `status`, `assignee_id`, `requester_id`, `priority`, and use search via `q`. I need to ensure the implementation is robust.

I need to focus on edge cases with the filters.  I am thinking through everything that can happen with each parameter.

*   **Status, priority** I've seen the pattern, valid values are only those specified in the enums, other values lead to 422. No surprises there.
*   **Assignee ID** I need to think VERY carefully here. What about `"unassigned"`? It represents `nil`, easy.  What about invalid IDs - negative, zero, non-numeric, or numbers bigger than the maximum size of an `Integer`? What about IDs that do NOT exist in the database, but are a valid integer? I've got to ensure the code handles this properly without leaking information about the existence of records in other accounts. Is a non-existent or foreign ID a 200 with an empty list, or a 422 validation error? I need to look closely at the existing tests, and the existing code in `TicketsController#parse_assignee_id` and existing validation to see how this is being handled in practice. If a non-existent ID matches no records, a 200 is appropriate (otherwise there is no way for a user to know that this attribute is causing a problem).
*   **Requester ID**  Similar concerns to `assignee_id`, must be a valid ID. I need to be careful with invalid requests.

**Deep Dive into Ticket Filtering**

Okay, this code has a consistent style, which is great. I'm focusing on the `assignee_id` and `requester_id` filtering logic, specifically in the `GET /api/v1/tickets` endpoint.

First, the `assignee_id` filter. If present and not blank, we have a few scenarios to consider.  If it's "unassigned", it's straightforward: we look for tickets where `assignee_id` is null. If not, the logic parses the `assignee_id` as a strict positive bigint ID using `parse_positive_bigint`. The key here is to handle the string representation of the ID, since that's what we get from query parameters. `parse_positive_bigint` validates the input string.  It needs to be a valid positive integer string.  The logic calls `parse_assignee_id`. Wait, it strips whitespace! So, something like `assignee_id=%20%20` gets caught as an invalid integer and errors. But why the difference between a 422 and a 200 empty result for a large bigint, like `"99999999999999999999999"`?

I need to compare the tests.  I expect that the same response code should apply for various invalid inputs:  `abc`, `0`, `-1`, and that extremely large bigint. A valid but non-existent ID also returns an empty result (200 OK with an empty array).  And for another account, it's also a 200 empty. The same behavior is expected for suspended staff, and customers.

Looking closer at `parse_assignee_id` it strips the whitespace in the `raw.strip`.  Then, if the raw is `"99999999999999999999999"` (too big), it returns `nil` and 422. It's a key part of the validation: reject malformed or too-large bigint strings, which matches tests. The tests include `"99999999999999999999999"` which should return 422. Also, inputs with leading/trailing spaces need to be rejected.

Wait, the logic in `parse_assignee_id` supports both `Integer` and `String` inputs. Very clean, and safe! In Rails integration tests, the query parameter is a String. And for both it needs to handle the range. `0`, `-1`, `"abc"`, `99999999999999999999999`, and `["1"]` or `{ a: "1" }` need to return 422.

Now for `requester_id`.  It's almost the same. But here's an important difference: `requester_id` *cannot* be "unassigned." Every ticket *must* have a requester. So, passing `"unassigned"` here *must* be an error and return 422. If the `requester_id` is a valid positive bigint, we filter accordingly. If the valid bigint ID is of another account, or non-existent, the query will return an empty result and a 200 OK. If the ID is invalid (like a malformed string, 0, or an extremely large number), it returns 422.

**Analyzing the Codebase and Search Implementation**

Okay, wow, this codebase is incredibly clean. The consistency is immediately apparent. I'm seeing a very well-defined pattern here that I appreciate. The handling of filter validation is exemplary:

*   Invalid enum values for filters like `status`, `priority`, `role`, and `suspended` are correctly flagged with a `422 Unprocessable Content` response, accompanied by `render_validation_errors(errors)`. Excellent.
*   Blank or missing filter values – either `nil` or an empty string (`""`) – are intelligently ignored, which is what I'd expect for optimal filter behavior. No action necessary, perfect.
*   Invalid `assignee_id` or `requester_id` values, such as non-positive bigints or, for `assignee_id`, something that isn't `"unassigned"`, are also triggering a `422 Unprocessable Content` with `render_validation_errors(errors)`. Good.
*   A valid, positive bigint `assignee_id` or `requester_id`, but one that doesn't match any tickets within the `current_account`, results in a graceful `200 OK` response with an empty `tickets` array and a `count` of 0. This is exactly what I would hope for, no errors returned here, just an accurate empty result.
*   The handling of multiple invalid filters within a single request is also spot on. They are correctly aggregated into an `errors = {}` hash, and `render_validation_errors(errors)` is called. Just like how `UsersController#index` handles it! This consistency is fantastic!

messages.content: Let's test `sanitize_sql_like`, `ILIKE ... ESCAPE '\'`, Unicode case-insensitivity, special characters (`%`, `_`, `\`, `'`, `.*`, etc.), and null bytes against our PostgreSQL database.
messages.thinking:
**Search Implementation Deep Dive**

Okay, so I'm thinking about this search functionality. The goal is to make it robust, efficient, and, above all, accurate. The core requirement is using `ILIKE` in PostgreSQL with `UTF-8` and C.UTF-8, which ensures case-insensitive matching that handles accented characters correctly. I need to test that `ILIKE` works perfectly with `ESCAPE '\'` and `ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like`.

The search needs to cover the ticket subject and public comments, ensuring that notes marked as "private" are *never* included. That's paramount. The prompt stresses that a private note should never influence a search, even if the public comments *do* contain the search term. Also, the search must avoid duplicates and handle the count and pagination precisely. I've concluded that the best approach is to use `EXISTS` to avoid duplicate rows and ensure accurate `count` and pagination. It's clean, efficient, and solves all of the potential issues with `LEFT OUTER JOIN`.

The key part is treating user input as literal text, which means escaping special SQL characters (`%`, `_`, `\`) and avoiding any SQL injection risks. That's why I'm focused on what `ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like` does and how PostgreSQL handles `ESCAPE '\'`. The escape character is crucial for correctly interpreting user input.

I need to consider all the `q` edge cases:

*   **Empty or Whitespace `q`**: An empty `q` or one containing only whitespace should return all tickets (unfiltered). Based on the context of the prompt, a search like `?q=%20%20%20` should return all results and is not a search for that string, it's just no search.
*   **Non-String `q`**: If `q` is an array or hash, the API should return a `422` with an error message, just like other similar controllers do.
*   **Null Byte `q`**: The system *must* handle null bytes (`\x00`) correctly, as PostgreSQL will raise an error when a null byte is encountered. This needs to be thoroughly tested.

In short: I want a search function that's rock-solid, secure, and intuitive for users.

cd /app && bin/rails runner '
conn = ActiveRecord::Base.connection

# Test sanitize_sql_like behavior
samples = ["receipt", "100%", "err_500", "a\\b", "\\%\\_", "O'\''Brien", "(foo|bar).*", "Café"]
samples.each do |s|
  escaped = ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like(s)
  puts "#{s.inspect} => #{escaped.inspect}"
end

# Test PG ILIKE with ESCAPE '\''\\'\''
tests = [
  ["100% off", "100%", true],
  ["1000 off", "100%", false],
  ["err_500", "err_500", true],
  ["errX500", "err_500", false],
  ["path C:\\Users\\Jo", "c:\\users", true],
  ["path C:UsersJo", "c:\\users", false],
  ["literal \\% sign", "\\%", true],
  ["literal % sign", "\\%", false],
  ["literal % sign", "%", true],
  ["anything without pct", "%", false],
  ["CAFÉ receipt", "café", true],
  ["café receipt", "CAFÉ", true],
  ["Cannot download my receipt", "RECEIPT", true],
  ["Cannot download my receipt", "ceipt", true],
  ["regex (a|b)+.*", "(a|b)+.*", true],
  ["regex a", "(a|b)+.*", false]
]

tests.each do |text, q, expected|
  pattern = "%#{ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like(q)}%"
  sql = ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_array(["SELECT ? ILIKE ? ESCAPE '\''\\\\'\'' AS matched", text, pattern])
  actual = conn.select_value(sql)
  status = (actual == expected) ? "OK" : "FAIL"
  puts "[#{status}] text=#{text.inspect} q=#{q.inspect} expected=#{expected} actual=#{actual}"
end

# Check what happens with null byte
begin
  pattern = "%#{ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like("foo\u0000bar")}%"
  sql = ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_array(["SELECT '\''foo'\'' ILIKE ? ESCAPE '\''\\\\'\''", pattern])
  puts "null byte result: #{conn.select_value(sql).inspect}"
rescue => e
  puts "null byte raised: #{e.class}: #{e.message}"
end
'

messages.thinking:
**The Backslash Blues: A PostgreSQL Escape Sequence Revelation**

Aha! Thank goodness we put that testing in place! It's paying off. I was just reviewing some PostgreSQL behavior, and it's a bit more nuanced than I initially realized, particularly with the `standard_conforming_strings = on` setting, which has been the default since version 9.1. It turns out that in SQL, `\\` actually represents *two* backslash characters. Trying to use `\\` for a single backslash? Nope, that throws a `PG::InvalidEscapeSequence` error. You know, that's not intuitive, but I get it.

The proper way to represent a single backslash literal in SQL is `'\'`. I'm already thinking about the implications for Ruby. In a double-quoted Ruby string, you'd need `"\\"` for that single backslash, and in a single quoted string or heredoc, the escape sequences are slightly simpler.

And here's the kicker: PostgreSQL, by default, already uses the backslash (`\`) as the escape character for `LIKE` and `ILIKE`! We can also explicitly define it as `ESCAPE '\'` (or its equivalent in Ruby strings, such as `"ESCAPE '\\'"`). I need to test that `ESCAPE '\'` usage thoroughly with `rails runner` to make sure it's behaving exactly as I expect. It's the only way to be sure.

rescue => e

end

messages.thinking:
**A Deep Dive into Query Parameters: Null Bytes, Whitespace, and Search Behavior**

Okay, so I just had a real "aha!" moment. That null byte error, right? `ArgumentError: string contains null byte`. If someone sends `/api/v1/tickets?q=foo%00bar`, and we pass that directly to Postgres, boom, 500. But wait! Postgres text columns *never* allow null bytes, so if the query *includes* a null byte, we have a few clean options. I think, `scope.none` is the winner! Return a 200 OK with an empty result set - it's semantically correct because no ticket can *literally* contain a null byte in its subject or comment, and it *prevents* a crash. And what about invalid UTF-8? Maybe check `!query.valid_encoding?` and return `scope.none` or a 422 if it is invalid encoding!

Now, onto the whitespace issue with the search query `q`. I need to figure out the behavior and what it means to strip whitespace or not. Let's look at `q=""`, `q="   "`, and `q="  receipt  "`. Blank query, no filter. Whitespace-only query, no filter. Trailing/leading spaces? If we `strip`, `"  receipt  "` is `"receipt"`. If we *don't* strip, it's literally `"  receipt  "`.

If someone searches "hello world" with strip, it is "hello world" and internal spaces are preserved, which is good. Does stripping preserve the internal spaces? Yep. What about "100%?" With strip, it will match "100% off." Is there any reasonable case where we *want* `"  receipt  "` to NOT match `"receipt"`? I cannot think of one. But, wait, what if someone tests for literal spaces? Both stripping and non-stripping keep internal spaces like `"download my."` What about `?q=   ` (blank whitespace)? Strip will treat it as no filter! `?q=   receipt   `? Strip finds "receipt!" Could someone test `" a "` and expect it to NOT match "cat"?

Honestly, I don't think so. In UI search inputs, `q.strip` is the standard approach, like in Rails `params[:q].strip` with `present?`/`blank?` treating whitespace-only as blank. Let's check this codebase: the `Account`, `User`, `Ticket` models, `BaseController`, and other controllers *all* strip whitespace from user-provided inputs. Everything treats whitespace-only strings as blank.

Okay, let's nail this down: if `raw_q` is `""` or `"   "`, `query.empty?` is true: no filter! `raw_q` is `"  receipt  "`, then `query` is `"receipt"` and it will match `"Cannot download my receipt"`. `"download my"` matches `"download my"` and finds "Cannot download my receipt." `"100%"` matches `"100% off."` Okay, I get it. This works! This is good. It's clean and safe!

And null bytes are gracefully handled now too! Is `Ticket.search_text(query)` the correct scope on `Ticket`? I think yes! Let's check how other models define scopes and see how they are implemented. Let's look at `app/models/invitation.rb` for some hints.

class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  include TokenDigestable

  INVITABLE_ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze
  EXPIRY = 7.days

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :sent_invitations

  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email,
    presence: true,
    length: { maximum: 255 },
    format: { with: User::EMAIL_FORMAT }
  validates :role, presence: true, inclusion: { in: INVITABLE_ROLES }
  validates :token_digest, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :expires_at, presence: true
  validate :invited_by_belongs_to_account
  validate :email_not_taken_by_existing_user, on: :create
  validate :no_competing_pending_invitation, on: :create

  scope :ordered_by_id, -> { order(id: :asc) }
  scope :pending, ->(at = Time.current) { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at > ?", at) }
  scope :accepted, -> { where.not(accepted_at: nil) }
  scope :revoked, -> { where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil) }
  scope :expired, ->(at = Time.current) { where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil).where("expires_at <= ?", at) }

  attr_accessor :raw_token

  def self.build_for(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:)
    raw = generate_raw_token
    invitation = account.invitations.build(
      invited_by: invited_by,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      token_digest: digest_token(raw),
      expires_at: EXPIRY.from_now
    )
    invitation.raw_token = raw
    invitation
  end

  def self.with_status(status, at: Time.current)
    case status
    when "pending" then pending(at)
    when "accepted" then accepted
    when "revoked" then revoked
    when "expired" then expired(at)
    else none
    end
  end

  def accepted?
    accepted_at.present?
  end

  def revoked?
    revoked_at.present?
  end

  def expired?(at: Time.current)
    !accepted? && !revoked? && expires_at <= at
  end

  def pending?(at: Time.current)
    !accepted? && !revoked? && expires_at > at
  end

  def status(at: Time.current)

Okay, let's take a look at this `sanitize_sql_like` method in Rails 8.1. It's surprisingly elegant, isn't it? It first doubles any backslashes (`\`) and then escapes any `%` or `_` characters with a backslash. Combined with PostgreSQL's `ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\'`, it ensures that every special character in the user's input is treated literally, while the outer `%...%` allows substring matching. Clean.

But wait a minute... looking at the comment directly below `sanitize_sql_like` in ActiveRecord is a game changer! It mentions escaping colons when using named bind variables. Since we're using `pattern: pattern` (named bind), and there are *no other* colons in our SQL fragment (`tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\' OR EXISTS (...)`), the `:pattern` named bind is completely unambiguous. The value of `:pattern` can contain colons, quotes, percent signs, *anything* – Rails binds it safely without parsing the value for potential bind variables! Brilliant! But, before I touch any of the controller code, I should double-check the `Ticket` model.

Hold on... I need to zoom in on this `search_text` method. There's a potential vulnerability here with invalid UTF-8 encoding. If `query` is a binary string with invalid UTF-8 bytes, and we call `.strip` on that string, Ruby will throw an `ArgumentError`. That's a classic example of an edge case causing grief! I need to ensure a more robust approach.

Okay, let's fix it by validating the encoding *before* stripping:

def self.search_text(query)
  raw = query.to_s
  return none unless raw.valid_encoding?

  term = raw.strip
  return all if term.empty?
  return none if term.include?("\x00")

Now, if `raw` has an invalid sequence, we return `none` cleanly, avoiding the error. If `raw` is empty, we return all tickets. If it has a null byte, we also return none. Otherwise, we can sanitize and perform the parameterized query.

Wait, another thought! What about the case where someone sends just whitespace? Like `%20` or `%20foo%20` versus just `foo`? I need to think about that. The search should treat the input literally. In a web app, `q=` and `q=%20%20` are both blank search queries; it's standard to return all records for that.

I need to make sure the tests cover these cases:

1.  `q = "   "` (whitespace only) -> Should return all records.
2.  `q = "a b"` -> Should match *exactly* `"a b"`.
3.  Also test other SQL injection and edge cases: `q = "100%"`, `q = "50_off"`, `q = "a\\b"`, `q = "%"`, `q = "_"`, `q = "\\"`, `q = "foo.*"`, `q = "foo|bar"`, `q = "foo & bar"`, `q = "-receipt"`, `q = '"receipt"'`, `q = "status:open"`, `q = "O'Brien"` (all literal, case-insensitive matches).

Alright, with that in mind, I'm ready to update `app/models/ticket.rb`, and then the controller files.

cd /app && cat <<'EOF' > app/models/ticket.rb
# frozen_string_literal: true

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets

  has_many :comments, class_name: "TicketComment", dependent: :delete_all, inverse_of: :ticket

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_is_active_staff_in_account, if: -> { assignee_id.present? && (new_record? || will_save_change_to_assignee_id?) }

  before_create :initialize_public_updated_at
  before_update :sync_public_updated_at

  scope :recently_active_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :recently_publicly_active_first, -> { order(public_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :with_status, ->(status) { where(status: status) }
  scope :with_priority, ->(priority) { where(priority: priority) }
  scope :unassigned, -> { where(assignee_id: nil) }
  scope :assigned_to, ->(assignee_id) { where(assignee_id: assignee_id) }
  scope :requested_by, ->(requester_id) { where(requester_id: requester_id) }

  def self.search_text(query)
    raw = query.to_s
    return none unless raw.valid_encoding?

    term = raw.strip
    return all if term.empty?
    return none if term.include?("\x00")

    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(term)}%"
    where(
      <<~'SQL'.squish,
        tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\'
        OR EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM ticket_comments
          WHERE ticket_comments.ticket_id = tickets.id
            AND ticket_comments.account_id = tickets.account_id
            AND ticket_comments.public = TRUE
            AND ticket_comments.body ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\'
        )
      SQL
      pattern: pattern
    )
  end

  def open?
    status == "open"
  end

  def pending?
    status == "pending"
  end

  def solved?
    status == "solved"
  end

  def normal_priority?
    priority == "normal"
  end

  def high_priority?
    priority == "high"
  end

  private

  def initialize_public_updated_at
    now = Time.current
    self.created_at ||= now
    self.updated_at ||= now
    self.public_updated_at ||= updated_at
  end

  def sync_public_updated_at
    return unless will_save_change_to_status? || will_save_change_to_subject?

    now = Time.current
    self.updated_at = now
    self.public_updated_at = now
  end

  def requester_belongs_to_account
    return unless requester && account_id

    if requester.account_id != account_id
      errors.add(:requester, "must belong to the same account")
    end
  end

  def assignee_is_active_staff_in_account
    return if assignee_id.nil?

    if assignee.nil? || assignee.account_id != account_id || !assignee.staff? || assignee.suspended?
      errors.add(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member in this account")
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class TicketTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @acme = Account.create!(name: "Acme", subdomain: "acme")
    @globex = Account.create!(name: "Globex", subdomain: "globex")

    @customer = @acme.users.create!(
      name: "Avery",
      email: "avery@example.test",
      password: "customer-password",
      role: "customer",
      email_verified_at: Time.current
    )
    @staff = @acme.users.create!(
      name: "Jo",
      email: "jo@acme.test",
      password: "staff-password",
      role: "admin",
      email_verified_at: Time.current
    )
    @agent = @acme.users.create!(
      name: "Sam",
      email: "sam@acme.test",
      password: "agent-password",
      role: "agent",
      email_verified_at: Time.current
    )
    @acme.update!(owner: @staff)

    @other_user = @globex.users.create!(
      name: "Other",
      email: "other@globex.test",
      password: "other-password",
      role: "customer",
      email_verified_at: Time.current
    )
    @other_staff = @globex.users.create!(
      name: "Other Staff",
      email: "staff@globex.test",
      password: "other-password",
      role: "admin",
      email_verified_at: Time.current
    )
  end

  test "validates subject, status, same-account requester, and active staff assignee" do
    ticket = @acme.tickets.build(requester: @customer, assignee: @agent, subject: "  Receipt issue  ")
    assert ticket.valid?
    assert_equal "open", ticket.status
    assert_equal "Receipt issue", ticket.subject

    blank_subject = @acme.tickets.build(requester: @customer, subject: "   ")
    assert_not blank_subject.valid?
    assert blank_subject.errors[:subject].any?

    invalid_status = @acme.tickets.build(requester: @customer, subject: "Help", status: "closed")
    assert_not invalid_status.valid?
    assert invalid_status.errors[:status].any?

    cross_account = @acme.tickets.build(requester: @other_user, subject: "Cross tenant")
    assert_not cross_account.valid?
    assert cross_account.errors[:requester].any?

    customer_assignee = @acme.tickets.build(requester: @customer, assignee: @customer, subject: "Bad assignee")
    assert_not customer_assignee.valid?
    assert customer_assignee.errors[:assignee_id].any?

    cross_staff_assignee = @acme.tickets.build(requester: @customer, assignee: @other_staff, subject: "Cross assignee")
    assert_not cross_staff_assignee.valid?
    assert cross_staff_assignee.errors[:assignee_id].any?

    @agent.suspend!
    suspended_assignee = @acme.tickets.build(requester: @customer, assignee: @agent, subject: "Suspended assignee")
    assert_not suspended_assignee.valid?
    assert suspended_assignee.errors[:assignee_id].any?
  end

  test "ticket comment validates body and same-account associations and tracks public vs internal activity" do
    ticket = @acme.tickets.create!(requester: @customer, subject: "Need help")

    blank_comment = TicketComment.new(account: @acme, ticket: ticket, author: @customer, body: "   ")
    assert_not blank_comment.valid?
    assert blank_comment.errors[:body].any?

    cross_author = TicketComment.new(account: @acme, ticket: ticket, author: @other_user, body: "Hi")
    assert_not cross_author.valid?
    assert cross_author.errors[:author].any?

    cross_account = TicketComment.new(account: @globex, ticket: ticket, author: @other_user, body: "Hi")
    assert_not cross_account.valid?
    assert cross_account.errors[:ticket].any?

    original_updated_at = ticket.updated_at
    original_public_updated_at = ticket.public_updated_at

    # Public comment touches both updated_at and public_updated_at
    travel 5.minutes do
      comment = TicketComment.create!(account: @acme, ticket: ticket, author: @staff, body: "Looking into it")
      assert_equal true, comment.public
      ticket.reload
      assert_operator ticket.updated_at, :>, original_updated_at
      assert_operator ticket.public_updated_at, :>, original_public_updated_at
    end

    after_public_updated_at = ticket.updated_at
    after_public_public_updated_at = ticket.public_updated_at

    # Private note touches updated_at only, NOT public_updated_at
    travel 10.minutes do
      note = TicketComment.create!(account: @acme, ticket: ticket, author: @staff, body: "Internal check", public: false)
      assert_equal false, note.public
      ticket.reload
      assert_operator ticket.updated_at, :>, after_public_updated_at
      assert_equal after_public_public_updated_at, ticket.public_updated_at
    end

    # Assignment change touches updated_at only, NOT public_updated_at
    travel 15.minutes do
      ticket.update!(assignee: @agent)
      ticket.reload
      assert_equal after_public_public_updated_at, ticket.public_updated_at
    end
  end

  test "purging an expired cancelled account also deletes its tickets and comments" do
    ticket = @acme.tickets.create!(requester: @customer, subject: "Receipt issue")
    comment = TicketComment.create!(account: @acme, ticket: ticket, author: @customer, body: "Cannot download")

    @acme.update!(cancelled_at: 91.days.ago)

    purged = Account.purge_expired_cancelled!
    assert_equal 1, purged
    assert_not Account.exists?(@acme.id)
    assert_not Ticket.exists?(ticket.id)
    assert_not TicketComment.exists?(comment.id)
  end
end

  test "staff filters tickets by status, assignee_id, requester_id, priority, and combined filters with pagination" do
    base_time = Time.utc(2026, 11, 20, 14, 0, 0)

    # Ticket in Globex that matches all filter values but MUST never appear in Acme
    globex_t = create_ticket_as(@globex_customer_token, subdomain: "globex", subject: "Globex receipt", body: "Globex receipt body", at: base_time + 5.minutes)
    patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{globex_t}",
      params: { ticket: { priority: "high" } },
      headers: account_headers("globex", token: @globex_owner_token),
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    # Configure Acme tickets:
    # t1: open,   unassigned,   high,   requester=avery, subject/body has "receipt"
    # t2: pending, assignee=sam, normal, requester=avery
    # t3: open,   assignee=jo,  high,   requester=blake, subject/body has "receipt"
    # t4: solved, unassigned,   normal, requester=blake
    # t5: open,   unassigned,   high,   requester=sam (staff!), body has "receipt"
    travel_to base_time + 10.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{t1}", params: { ticket: { priority: "high" } }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token), as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end
    travel_to base_time + 11.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{t2}", params: { ticket: { status: "pending", assignee_id: @agent.id } }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token), as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end
    travel_to base_time + 12.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{t3}", params: { ticket: { priority: "high", assignee_id: @owner.id } }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token), as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end
    travel_to base_time + 13.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{t4}", params: { ticket: { status: "solved" } }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token), as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end
    travel_to base_time + 14.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{t5}", params: { ticket: { priority: "high" } }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token), as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    # Status filters

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t5, t3, t1 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }
    assert_equal 3, json_body["count"]

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { status: "pending" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @agent_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t2 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { status: "solved" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @agent_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t4 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    # Priority filters
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { priority: "high" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @agent_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t5, t3, t1 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { priority: "normal" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @agent_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t4, t2 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    # Assignee filters (unassigned, specific staff, non-matching valid IDs)
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { assignee_id: "unassigned" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t5, t4, t1 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { assignee_id: @agent.id }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t2 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { assignee_id: @owner.id }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t3 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    # Valid bigint IDs with no matches (nonexistent, customer, cross-tenant staff) return 200 empty
    [ 999_999, @avery.id, @globex_owner.id ].each do |id|
      get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { assignee_id: id }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :ok
      assert_equal [], json_body["tickets"]
      assert_equal 0, json_body["count"]
    end

    # Requester filters (customers and staff-as-requester)
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { requester_id: @avery.id }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t2, t1 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { requester_id: @blake.id }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t4, t3 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { requester_id: @agent.id }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t5 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    # Cross-tenant requester returns 200 empty
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { requester_id: @globex_customer.id }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [], json_body["tickets"]
    assert_equal 0, json_body["count"]

    # Combined filter matching prompt example: status + assignee_id=unassigned + priority + q
    get "/api/v1/tickets?status=open&assignee_id=unassigned&priority=high&q=receipt",
      headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)

    assert_equal [ t5, t1 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]

    # Combine all 5 filters including requester_id
    get "/api/v1/tickets",
      params: { status: "open", assignee_id: "unassigned", requester_id: @avery.id, priority: "high", q: "receipt" },
      headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t1 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]

    # Combined filters + pagination
    get "/api/v1/tickets",
      params: { status: "open", priority: "high", page: 1, per_page: 2 },
      headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t5, t3 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }
    assert_equal 3, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal 2, json_body["next_page"]

    get "/api/v1/tickets",

    assert_equal [ t1 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }
    assert_equal 3, json_body["count"]
    assert_nil json_body["next_page"]
    assert_equal 1, json_body["previous_page"]

    # Empty query params are ignored
    get "/api/v1/tickets?status=&priority=&assignee_id=&requester_id=&q=",
      headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 5, json_body["count"]

    # Suspending an assigned agent unassigns their tickets so they appear under assignee_id=unassigned
    patch "/api/v1/users/#{@agent.id}",
      params: { user: { suspended: true } },
      headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token),
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { assignee_id: @agent.id }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [], json_body["tickets"]

    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { assignee_id: "unassigned", status: "pending" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t2 ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

  test "staff search q is case-insensitive, searches subjects and public comments only, deduplicates, and treats input literally" do
    base_time = Time.utc(2026, 11, 20, 15, 0, 0)

    # t_subject: matches in subject AND multiple public comments (tests deduplication)
    t_subject = create_ticket_as(@avery_token, subject: "Cannot download my RECEIPT", body: "First receipt comment", at: base_time)
    travel_to base_time + 1.minute do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{t_subject}",
        params: { ticket: { comment: { body: "Staff public reply about Receipt #1", public: true } } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", token: @agent_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end
    travel_to base_time + 2.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/requests/#{t_subject}",
        params: { request: { comment: { body: "Customer follow-up about receipt #2" } } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    # t_public_comment: only matches via a staff public comment (not subject)
    t_public_comment = create_ticket_as(@avery_token, subject: "Billing inquiry", body: "General question", at: base_time + 3.minutes)
    travel_to base_time + 4.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{t_public_comment}",
        params: { ticket: { comment: { body: "Here is your updated Café Receipt PDF", public: true } } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    # t_private_only: "receipt" and "secret_token" appear ONLY in private note (MUST NOT match!)
    t_private_only = create_ticket_as(@blake_token, subject: "General support", body: "Nothing special here", at: base_time + 5.minutes)
    travel_to base_time + 6.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{t_private_only}",
        params: { ticket: { comment: { body: "Internal note: check receipt and secret_token 100%", public: false } } },
        headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    # t_special: literal wildcard, backslash, regex, SQL, and operator characters
    t_special = create_ticket_as(
      @blake_token,
      subject: '100% discount code err_500 on C:\Users\Blake',
      body: %q{Literal chars: \% and (foo|bar).* and [a-z]+ and ' OR '1'='1 -- and -receipt and status:open},
      at: base_time + 7.minutes
    )

    # t_decoy: would match if % or _ or .* or \ were treated as wildcards/regex instead of literal text
    t_decoy = create_ticket_as(
      @blake_token,
      subject: "1000 discount code errX500 on C:UsersBlake",
      body: "Just foo and a and my download order",
      at: base_time + 8.minutes
    )

    # Globex ticket with "receipt" must never match in Acme
    create_ticket_as(@globex_customer_token, subdomain: "globex", subject: "Globex receipt", body: "Globex receipt", at: base_time + 9.minutes)

    # 1. Case-insensitive search through subjects and public comments, excludes private notes, no duplicates
    [ "receipt", "RECEIPT", "ReCeIpT", "ceipt", "  receipt  " ].each do |term|
      get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: term }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :ok, "Failed for q=#{term.inspect}"
      assert_equal [ t_special, t_public_comment, t_subject ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }, "Mismatch for q=#{term.inspect}"
      assert_equal 3, json_body["count"]
    end

    # 2. Private-only term returns nothing
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "secret_token" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [], json_body["tickets"]
    assert_equal 0, json_body["count"]

    # 3. Unicode case-insensitive search
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "CAFÉ" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ t_public_comment ], json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }

    # 4. Literal text search for LIKE wildcards (%, _, \), regex, SQL chars, and search operators
    {
      "%" => [ t_special ],
      "100%" => [ t_special ],
      "_" => [ t_special ],
      "err_500" => [ t_special ],
      "ERR_500" => [ t_special ],
      '\\' => [ t_special ],
      'c:\users\blake' => [ t_special ],
      '\%' => [ t_special ],
      "(foo|bar).*" => [ t_special ],
      "[a-z]+" => [ t_special ],
      "' OR '1'='1 --" => [ t_special ],
      "-receipt" => [ t_special ],
      "status:open" => [ t_special ],
      "download my" => [ t_subject ],
      "my download" => [ t_decoy ]
    }.each do |query, expected_ids|
      get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: query }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :ok, "Expected 200 for q=#{query.inspect}"
      assert_equal expected_ids, json_body["tickets"].map { |t| t["id"] }, "Expected #{expected_ids.inspect} for q=#{query.inspect}"
      assert_equal expected_ids.size, json_body["count"]
    end

    # 5. Blank/whitespace-only q returns all tickets unfiltered
    get "/api/v1/tickets", params: { q: "   " }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 5, json_body["count"]

    # 6. Null byte in q returns 200 empty cleanly (no 500)
    get "/api/v1/tickets?q=receipt%00test", headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [], json_body["tickets"]
    assert_equal 0, json_body["count"]
  end

  test "invalid filter values on GET /api/v1/tickets return 422 cleanly" do
    invalid_queries = [
      [ { status: "closed" }, "status" ],
      [ { status: "OPEN" }, "status" ],
      [ { status: "   " }, "status" ],
      [ { status: [ "open" ] }, "status" ],
      [ { priority: "urgent" }, "priority" ],
      [ { priority: "HIGH" }, "priority" ],
      [ { priority: "   " }, "priority" ],
      [ { priority: [ "high" ] }, "priority" ],
      [ { assignee_id: "UNASSIGNED" }, "assignee_id" ],
      [ { assignee_id: "none" }, "assignee_id" ],
      [ { assignee_id: "abc" }, "assignee_id" ],
      [ { assignee_id: "0" }, "assignee_id" ],
      [ { assignee_id: "-1" }, "assignee_id" ],
      [ { assignee_id: "01" }, "assignee_id" ],
      [ { assignee_id: "99999999999999999999999" }, "assignee_id" ],
      [ { assignee_id: [ "1" ] }, "assignee_id" ],
      [ { requester_id: "unassigned" }, "requester_id" ],
      [ { requester_id: "abc" }, "requester_id" ],
      [ { requester_id: "0" }, "requester_id" ],
      [ { requester_id: "-5" }, "requester_id" ],
      [ { requester_id: "99999999999999999999999" }, "requester_id" ],
      [ { requester_id: [ "1" ] }, "requester_id" ],
      [ { q: [ "receipt" ] }, "q" ],
      [ { q: { term: "receipt" } }, "q" ]
    ]

    invalid_queries.each do |params_hash, error_key|
      get "/api/v1/tickets", params: params_hash, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content, "Expected 422 for #{params_hash.inspect}"
      assert_equal "validation_failed", json_body["code"]
      assert json_body.dig("errors", error_key).present?, "Expected errors.#{error_key} for #{params_hash.inspect}"
    end

    # Multiple invalid filters return all errors together
    get "/api/v1/tickets",
      params: { status: "bad", priority: "bad", assignee_id: "bad", requester_id: "bad" },
      headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
    %w[status priority assignee_id requester_id].each do |key|
      assert json_body.dig("errors", key).present?, "Expected errors.#{key}"

  end

  test "customers can filter their own requests by status and cannot filter or infer internal priority" do
    base_time = Time.utc(2026, 11, 20, 16, 0, 0)

    a_open_1 = create_ticket_as(@avery_token, subject: "Avery open 1", body: "Body 1", at: base_time)
    a_open_2 = create_ticket_as(@avery_token, subject: "Avery open 2", body: "Body 2", at: base_time + 1.minute)
    a_pending = create_ticket_as(@avery_token, subject: "Avery pending", body: "Body 3", at: base_time + 2.minutes)
    a_solved = create_ticket_as(@avery_token, subject: "Avery solved", body: "Body 4", at: base_time + 3.minutes)
    b_open = create_ticket_as(@blake_token, subject: "Blake open", body: "Body 5", at: base_time + 4.minutes)

    # Set statuses & internal priorities
    travel_to base_time + 10.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{a_open_1}", params: { ticket: { priority: "high" } }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token), as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end
    travel_to base_time + 11.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{a_pending}", params: { ticket: { status: "pending", priority: "high" } }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token), as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end
    travel_to base_time + 12.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{a_solved}", params: { ticket: { status: "solved" } }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @owner_token), as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    # Avery filters own requests by status (open preserves public_updated_at order despite high priority edit on a_open_1!)
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ a_open_2, a_open_1 ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]
    json_body["requests"].each { |r| assert_not r.key?("priority") }

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "pending" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ a_pending ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "solved" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ a_solved ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 1, json_body["count"]

    # Empty status returns all of Avery's requests (never Blake's)
    get "/api/v1/requests?status=", headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 4, json_body["count"]
    assert_not_includes json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }, b_open

    # Pagination with status filter
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open", page: 1, per_page: 1 }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ a_open_2 ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal 2, json_body["next_page"]

    # Priority/assignee/requester params on /requests are ignored so customers cannot probe internal fields or other users
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { priority: "high" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 4, json_body["count"]

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open", priority: "high" }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [ a_open_2, a_open_1 ], json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { requester_id: @blake.id }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 4, json_body["count"]
    assert_not_includes json_body["requests"].map { |r| r["id"] }, b_open

    # Invalid status values on GET /requests return 422
    [ "closed", "OPEN", "   ", [ "open" ], { a: "open" } ].each do |bad_status|
      get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: bad_status }, headers: account_headers("acme", token: @avery_token)
      assert_response :unprocessable_content, "Expected 422 for customer status=#{bad_status.inspect}"
      assert json_body.dig("errors", "status").present?
    end
  end

  private

  def create_ticket_as(token, subject:, body:, at:, subdomain: "acme")
    ticket_id = nil
    travel_to at do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: subject, comment: { body: body } } },
        headers: account_headers(subdomain, token: token),
        as: :json
      assert_response :created
      ticket_id = json_body.dig("request", "id")
    end
    ticket_id
  end
end

First, I need to verify what happens when the migration is run on a database containing tickets. I'm going to roll back, insert a ticket without the priority column, rerun the migration, and confirm the existing rows correctly get the default priority of "normal." That's crucial for a clean upgrade path.

Next, how does the API handle malformed UTF-8 in the `q` parameter? I'll need to hit the Rails app with some `%FF%FE` sequences and see what Puma or the integration tests actually return in an HTTP request. This is important for security and data handling.

I'll also test the `GET /api/v1/tickets` endpoint using a live Puma server and `curl`. I need to confirm correct URL-encoded special characters like `%25`, `%5C`, `_`, and `%20` are handled consistently for the `q` filter, and other query params too.

Hold on, about that `q` filter... I need to *really* think this through. What if a ticket subject has internal spaces? For instance, what if there's a ticket with "hello   world" (three spaces) and someone searches for that exactly? My testing shows that `.strip` *doesn't* collapse internal spaces. It's great that internal spaces are preserved literally. But I want to make sure I understand the interaction perfectly.

Now, let's look at `assignee_id` and `requester_id` with leading/trailing spaces. Like `%2042%20` or `%20unassigned%20`. I'm going to dig into the code and see that `parse_positive_bigint` correctly handles the stripping, and what's interesting, the behavior is now predictable and correct - `assignee_id=42` does not have spaces, `assignee_id=%20%20` (whitespace only) becomes `""` which fails and returns 422.

Time to look at `status` and `priority`. Let's verify not just array params, but also hash params. I know how Rails's strong params work, so making sure a hash `422 Unprocessable Content` is returned is essential.

I'm checking security, now. How are requests handled with canceled accounts, unauthenticated users, or customers? Now for performance: what about that `q` search parameter with a *massive* string, say 10,000 characters? I'm reassured knowing that PostgreSQL's `ILIKE` is handling this safely, without the risks of regex backtracking.

Finally, I need to check for consistency. I'm going to inspect `UsersController#index`, `TicketsController#index`, and `RequestsController#index`. I'm going to compare the usage of the `filter_param_present?` helper. I need to make sure the key checking convention is used the same everywhere. messages.content: Let's run a live end-to-end verification against Puma using `curl` (against the test database on an ephemeral port so we don't pollute development DB), testing the exact prompt URL and special characters over HTTP.
messages.thinking:
Okay, here's my understanding, tailored for an expert audience, as a first-person account of the thought process:

**Verification Complete: UTF-8, Rollbacks, and Live Server Testing**

Alright, that's great! The validation for invalid UTF-8 characters is behaving exactly as expected, throwing a clean 400 Bad Request error. Excellent, exactly what we needed! And the migration process seems completely robust – rollbacks and re-migrations are working flawlessly in both the development and test environments. No database corruption or unexpected behaviors there.

Now, to make sure this all holds water in a real-world scenario, I'm thinking we need a live test. Specifically, let's hit a live Puma HTTP server with `curl`. This is where the rubber meets the road. I want to verify the entire stack – the HTTP headers, the JSON responses (making sure they're properly formatted, of course), how the URL query strings are encoded and decoded, and most importantly, that `curl` returns the *exact* expected prompt endpoint `GET /api/v1/tickets?status=open&assignee_id=unassigned&priority=high&q=receipt`.

Finally, after the live server check, we need to tidy up the development database. It's a good practice to avoid any residual data. We don't want any unexpected interactions in future tests, or confusion amongst the team.

arguments.command:
cd /app && bash -c '
set -euo pipefail
PORT=3099
RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails server -p $PORT -b 127.0.0.1 >/tmp/puma_verify.log 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!
trap "kill $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true; wait $SERVER_PID 2>/dev/null || true; RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails runner \"Account.where(subdomain: '\''verifyacme'\'').destroy_all\" 2>/dev/null || true" EXIT

for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/up >/dev/null; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.2
done

# Seed test account, staff, customer, tickets via Rails runner in test DB
TOKENS=$(RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails runner "
Account.where(subdomain: '\''verifyacme'\'').destroy_all
acc = Account.create!(name: '\''Verify Acme'\'', subdomain: '\''verifyacme'\'')
owner = acc.users.create!(name: '\''Jo'\'', email: '\''jo@verify.test'\'', password: '\''password123'\'', role: '\''admin'\'', email_verified_at: Time.current)
acc.update!(owner: owner)
cust = acc.users.create!(name: '\''Avery'\'', email: '\''avery@verify.test'\'', password: '\''password123'\'', role: '\''customer'\'', email_verified_at: Time.current)

owner_sess = Session.issue_for!(owner)
cust_sess = Session.issue_for!(cust)

puts \"#{owner_sess.raw_token} #{cust_sess.raw_token} #{owner.id} #{cust.id}\"
")
read -r OWNER_TOKEN CUST_TOKEN OWNER_ID CUST_ID <<< "$TOKENS"

# 1. Customer creates two requests
T1=$(curl -sf -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/v1/requests \
  -H "X-Helpdesk-Account: verifyacme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUST_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '\''{"request":{"subject":"Cannot download 100% receipt","comment":{"body":"Please send PDF receipt"}}}'\'' | ruby -rjson -e "d=JSON.parse(STDIN.read); raise '\''priority leaked!'\'' if d['\''request'\''].key?('\''priority'\''); puts d['\''request'\'']['\''id'\'']")

T2=$(curl -sf -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/v1/requests \
  -H "X-Helpdesk-Account: verifyacme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUST_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '\''{"request":{"subject":"Other question 1000","comment":{"body":"General help"}}}'\'' | ruby -rjson -e "d=JSON.parse(STDIN.read); puts d['\''request'\'']['\''id'\'']")

# 2. Staff marks T1 high priority and T2 pending with private note mentioning receipt
curl -sf -X PATCH http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/v1/tickets/$T1 \
  -H "X-Helpdesk-Account: verifyacme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OWNER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '\''{"ticket":{"priority":"high"}}'\'' | ruby -rjson -e "d=JSON.parse(STDIN.read); raise '\''wrong priority'\'' unless d['\''ticket'\'']['\''priority'\''] == '\''high'\''; puts '\''T1 updated to high'\''"

curl -sf -X PATCH http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/v1/tickets/$T2 \
  -H "X-Helpdesk-Account: verifyacme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OWNER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '\''{"ticket":{"status":"pending","comment":{"body":"Internal receipt note","public":false}}}'\'' >/dev/null

# 3. Exact prompt query
curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/v1/tickets?status=open&assignee_id=unassigned&priority=high&q=receipt" \
  -H "X-Helpdesk-Account: verifyacme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OWNER_TOKEN" | ruby -rjson -e "d=JSON.parse(STDIN.read); ids=d['\''tickets'\''].map{|t| t['\''id'\'']}; raise \"Unexpected: #{d}\" unless ids == [$T1] && d['\''count'\''] == 1; puts '\''Exact prompt query OK: '\'' + ids.inspect"

# 4. Literal percent over HTTP (%25)
curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/v1/tickets?q=100%25" \
  -H "X-Helpdesk-Account: verifyacme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OWNER_TOKEN" | ruby -rjson -e "d=JSON.parse(STDIN.read); ids=d['\''tickets'\''].map{|t| t['\''id'\'']}; raise \"Unexpected: #{d}\" unless ids == [$T1]; puts '\''Literal 100% over HTTP OK'\''"

# 5. Customer status filter
curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/api/v1/requests?status=pending" \
  -H "X-Helpdesk-Account: verifyacme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUST_TOKEN" | ruby -rjson -e "d=JSON.parse(STDIN.read); ids=d['\''requests'\''].map{|r| r['\''id'\'']}; raise \"Unexpected: #{d}\" unless ids == [$T2] && !d['\''requests'\''].first.key?('\''priority'\''); puts '\''Customer status filter OK'\''"

echo "ALL LIVE HTTP CHECKS PASSED!"
'
